description: Use this when the user wants to draw a raffle winner, pick random winners from ticket numbers or names, or use a raffle number generator with no repeats. Draws winners (and optional alternates) without replacement with a secure random number generator from a range such as 1-500, several sold ranges, or a list of names (a name listed twice has two entries); can exclude numbers and assign prizes in draw order. Returns the ordered winners and a draw log PDF and CSV with time, method, entry count and an entry-list fingerprint. Each call is a new draw, so do not call it again to change a result. Does not sell tickets or take payments, and is not legal advice: raffle rules vary by place.

alternates.description: Backup winners drawn after the winners, in order, for unclaimed prizes. Default 0.

entries.description: What is in the drum: sold ticket numbers, ranges or names, as a list or pasted lines. Ranges like 1-250 or A-0001 to A-0100 are expanded. A name listed 3 times has 3 entries. Example: "1-250, 301-420" or ["Ava Patel", "Liam Chen", "Ava Patel"].

event_name.description: Event name for the draw log, e.g. Spring Gala Raffle.

exclude.description: Numbers or names to leave out before the draw, e.g. void tickets or earlier winners: "17, 42".

first_number.description: Instead of entries: the first ticket number of a range, e.g. 1.

last_number.description: Instead of entries: the last ticket number of a range, e.g. 500.

one_prize_per_person.description: With names: skip further entries of someone who already won. Default true.

prizes.description: Prizes in draw order; the first winner gets the first prize. Example: ["TV", "Gift card", "Mug"].

winners.description: How many winners to draw, 1 to 100. Default 1, or the number of prizes when prizes are given.

name: draw_raffle_winners
title: Draw raffle winners
